transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Well, my family actually brought me in today. I guess... I guess I caused a bit of a fuss at the county fair, which I feel just terrible about. I hope you don't think too badly of me, but... I was giving a talk about the equipment, and I climbed up onto the tractor. I just wanted to show the crowd this new pattern I'd figured out. I was jerking the controls around to demonstrate it to them, and... well, I just couldn't seem to make myself stop doing it, even when folks started yelling at me to get down. 

I know it probably looked really strange, and I'm usually much more professional than that, I promise. I really didn't mean to cause any trouble. Does that make sense why they'd want me to come see you?
What was going through your mind, or what kind of feeling did you have, that made it so hard to stop jerking the controls?

Well... it's awfully embarrassing to try and explain, to be honest with you. I hope you don't think I'm losing my marbles or anything. 

It was just... I had this 'new pattern' figured out, you see? And once I climbed up there during my talk and started jerking the levers to show the crowd... it was like I just had to keep doing it. I don't exactly know how to describe the feeling, but even with everybody hollering at me to get down, I just... I couldn't seem to make my hands quit moving those controls. It was like my body was just stuck doing it, if that makes any sense? 

I know it must have looked so foolish for a man my age to be acting like that. I really do try to be a good, respectable representative for the agricultural board, I promise you. Do you... do you think maybe I was just a little overly excited?
Recently, have you found yourself needing less sleep than usual while still having plenty of energy?

Well, I... I suppose my sleep hasn't been quite what you'd call normal lately, but I really don't mind it. I hope that's alright to say. 

It's just that, well, most nights I'll only doze for maybe two or three hours in my armchair, or sometimes I just don't sleep at all. But the funny thing is, I'm up before the sun, and I feel completely charged up. I'm out the door and ready to work the whole place like I had a full eight hours. 

I know folks say you need your rest at my age, but I've just been feeling so productive. Getting a lot done around the farm, you know? I hope you don't think it's a bad thing that I've been so energetic on so little sleep... is it okay that I've been feeling that way?
Before this recent period, have you ever experienced a time in your life when you felt deeply depressed or down for weeks at a time?

Oh, well... no, I don't think so. I mean, everybody gets a little blue sometimes, right? Especially when the crops don't yield like you hoped, or... or a piece of machinery breaks down. That's just normal life, I think. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, Doctor. I've always been the type to just pull my boots on and get back to work, no matter what. I don't think I've ever let myself get stuck in a rut for weeks at a time like that. I'm usually pretty good at just... shaking it off, you know? 

I hope that's the right answer. I mean, I wouldn't want you to think I'm the sort of fellow who just sits around feeling sorry for himself. I'm a hard worker, I promise. Does that... does that sound about right to you?
Aside from the fair, has this burst of energy caused any serious problems or disruptions with your day-to-day work or relationships?

Well... I mean, I wouldn't call them *serious* problems, exactly. Just... a few adjustments, I suppose. I hope you don't think I'm a burden on my family or anything. 

It's just that, well... my wife and some of the hands have sort of... stepped up to help out with some of the decisions I usually handle. Just temporarily, you know? Like with the lenders and... and deciding when to run certain equipment. They just felt like maybe it wasn't the safest idea for me to be in charge of the daily operations right now, especially after what happened at the fair. 

I guess... well, I guess that incident made some folks a little nervous about whether I could keep running the farm the way I always have. But I'm sure it'll all blow over soon, right? I mean, it's perfectly normal for a family to pitch in when someone's feeling a little... over-eager, wouldn't you say? I really do want to get back to pulling my own weight, Doctor. I promise I'm not trying to shirk my responsibilities.
